title: faunal-diversity Mindmap
notes: Protozoa are animal-like, mostly unicellular eukaryotes classified by their locomotion into four classes: Sarcodina (pseudopodia, e.g. Amoeba), Mastigophora…
**Protista:** unicellular eukaryotes. Includes protozoa (animal-like), algae (plant-like) and slime moulds (fungus-like).
**Protozoa characteristics:** unicellular, eukaryotic, heterotrophic, locomotion by cilia, flagella or pseudopodia, reproduce by binary fission or multiple…

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Protista: eukaryotic, mostly unicellular; animal/plant/fungus-like.
Protozoa = animal-like; locomotion defines the 4 classes.
Sarcodina (Amoeba) — pseudopodia; Ciliophora (Paramecium) — cilia.
Mastigophora (Trypanosoma) — flagella; Sporozoa (Plasmodium) — non-motile spores.
Paramecium has two nuclei (macro + micro) and contractile vacuoles.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Protozoa classes: Sarcodina (pseudopodia), Mastigophora (flagella), Ciliophora (cilia), Sporozoa…
Amoeba: cell membrane + cytoplasm + nucleus + food vacuole + contractile vacuole
Paramecium: cilia + oral groove + food vacuole + macro/micronucleus + contractile vacuole

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Protozoa are animal-like protists that move by pseudopodia, flagella, or cilia.
Paramecium is ciliated and has two distinct nuclei.
Plasmodium (a sporozoan) causes malaria and requires the Anopheles mosquito as its vector.

subtopics.name: Exam focus
points: Draw and label Paramecium — very common.
Tabulate the 4 Protozoa classes (locomotion, example, disease).
Explain the Plasmodium life cycle with Anopheles.
Protozoa = Proto (first) + zoon (animal).
Amoeba = pseudo (false foot) = pseudopodia.

subtopics.name: Common misconceptions
points: Protists are eukaryotes (have a nucleus); they are NOT bacteria (prokaryotes).
Protozoa are animal-like; algae are plant-like; slime moulds are fungus-like — all are in Protista.
Amoeba moves by pseudopodia (no flagella/cilia); Paramecium by cilia; Trypanosoma by flagella.

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Levels: cellular (Porifera) → tissue (Cnidaria) → organ system (higher).
Body cavity: acoelom, pseudocoelom, coelom.
Symmetry: asymmetry, radial, bilateral.
Segmentation in Annelida, Arthropoda, Chordata.
9 phyla: Porifera, Cnidaria, Platyhelminthes, Nematoda, Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Echinodermata,…

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Body cavity: Acoelom (no cavity) / Pseudocoelom (partly lined) / Coelom (fully mesoderm-lined)
Symmetry: Asymmetry (Porifera) / Radial (Cnidaria, Echinodermata) / Bilateral (Platyhelminthes onward)
Chordate features: notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, post-anal tail

subtopics.name: Statements to quote
points: Animal organisation progresses from cellular (Porifera) to organ-system (Chordata).
Body cavity type (acoelom/pseudocoelom/coelom) is a key evolutionary feature.
Chordates are defined by four shared features: notochord, dorsal nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, post-anal tail.

subtopics.name: Exam focus

Chordate = C-D-P-P (Chordate, Dorsal nerve, Pharyngeal slits, post-anal tail).
